import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ratio of product of GCDs to product of factorials of floor divisions

$$a(n) = \frac{\prod_{j=1}^n \prod_{k=1}^n \gcd(j,k)}{\prod_{k=1}^n (\lfloor n/k \rfloor!)^k}$$

*References:*
- [A129365](https://oeis.org/A129365)
-/

namespace OeisA129365

/-- $a(n) = \frac{\prod_{j=1}^n \prod_{k=1}^n \gcd(j,k)}{\prod_{k=1}^n (\lfloor n/k \rfloor!)^k}$. -/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  let num : ℚ := (Finset.Icc 1 n).prod fun j => (Finset.Icc 1 n).prod fun k => Nat.gcd j k
  let den : ℚ := (Finset.Icc 1 n).prod fun k => (n / k).factorial ^ k
  num / den

/-- Sequence A004125: sum of remainders $n \bmod k$ for $1 \le k \le n$. -/
def b (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, (n % k)

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 0. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by decide +native

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 1. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by decide +native

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 1 := by decide +native

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 3. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 1 := by decide +native

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 4. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 1 := by decide +native

/--
Conjecture (1): $a(n)$ is always an integer (the denominator divides the numerator).

Answer: true, see linked proof.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/oeis-a129365-conjectures/blob/9c0201540c337733d6b8afb2aff209f5489c122a/lean/OeisA129365FC.lean#L234-L395"]
theorem conjecture1 (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    ((Finset.Icc 1 n).prod fun k => (n / k).factorial ^ k) ∣
      ((Finset.Icc 1 n).prod fun j => (Finset.Icc 1 n).prod fun k => Nat.gcd j k) := by
  sorry

/--
Conjecture (2): If $p$ is a prime, then $p \mid a(n)$ if and only if $p \le n/3$.

Answer: true, see linked proof.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/oeis-a129365-conjectures/blob/9c0201540c337733d6b8afb2aff209f5489c122a/lean/OeisA129365FC.lean#L234-L395"]
theorem conjecture2 (n p : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hp : p.Prime) :
    (∃ m : ℕ, a n = m ∧ p ∣ m) ↔ p ≤ n / 3 := by
  sorry

/--
Conjecture (3): For each positive integer $n$, prime $p$, and $0 \le k < p$,
$\mathrm{ord}_p(a(np)) = \mathrm{ord}_p(a(np + k))$.

Answer: true, see linked proof.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/oeis-a129365-conjectures/blob/9c0201540c337733d6b8afb2aff209f5489c122a/lean/OeisA129365FC.lean#L234-L395"]
theorem conjecture3 (n p k : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hp : p.Prime) (hk : k < p) :
    padicValRat p (a (n * p)) = padicValRat p (a (n * p + k)) := by
  sorry

/--
Conjecture (4): Let $b(n) = \mathrm{A004125}(n) = \sum_{k=1}^n (n \bmod k)$. Then
$\mathrm{ord}_p(a(np)) = \sum_{i \ge 0} b(\lfloor n/p^i \rfloor)$.

Answer: true, see linked proof.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/oeis-a129365-conjectures/blob/9c0201540c337733d6b8afb2aff209f5489c122a/lean/OeisA129365FC.lean#L234-L395"]
theorem conjecture4 (n p : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hp : p.Prime) :
    padicValRat p (a (n * p)) = ∑' i : ℕ, (b (n / p ^ i) : ℤ) := by
  sorry

end OeisA129365

reformulations.difference: OEIS conjecture A asserts that a(n) is an integer. Lean instead asserts natural-number divisibility of the displayed numerator by the displayed denominator.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing N and D for the two natural-number products, D is strictly positive and a(n) = (N : ℚ)/(D : ℚ). Consequently D ∣ N if and only if there exists z : ℤ with a(n) = z. This exact equivalence was proved in ReviewA129365.conjecture1_reformulation without using any of the conjecture declarations.

reformulations.difference: Lean expresses p | a(n) using a natural-number witness for a(n), and interprets n / 3 as natural-number division.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Since a(n) > 0 and a prime p is positive, (∃ m : ℕ, a(n) = m ∧ p ∣ m) is equivalent to a(n) being an integer multiple of p. Also p ≤ ⌊n/3⌋ is equivalent to 3p ≤ n, hence to p ≤ n/3 with rational division. The full equivalence to the integer-multiple formulation with the rational bound was proved in ReviewA129365.conjecture2_reformulation, independently of the conjecture declarations.

review.notes:
Checked both definitions, all five tests, and all four conjectures. OEIS HTML requests were blocked, so the complete official OEIS database entries were read instead. All 27 displayed terms of A129365 match Lean computations. Additional small-case checks of all four claims pass; the five test equalities were also independently kernel-checked.

The scratch file /workspace/review/scratch.lean proves a(n) > 0 and proves that the sum in conjecture4 has zero terms for i > Nat.log p n. Thus neither the valuation-at-zero convention nor the divergent-tsum default changes these statements. The extensions a(0) = 1 and b(0) = 0 agree with the empty-product and empty-sum formulas.

The exact cited external proof compiles against this checkout. Each of its four theorem proofs depends only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, with no sorryAx. The research-solved tags and formal-proof records are therefore supported. No declarations remain unverified.
